frontend/apps/mobile/src/voice/VoiceAssistant.ts:79-101 - startListening() guards with `if (this.state !== 'idle') return;` (L80-82). On a native failure it sets `this.updateState('error')` (L85 and L98) and rethrows/throws. There is NO code path anywhere in the class that transitions state from 'error' back to 'idle': the only resets to 'idle' are stopListening() (L115, reachable only from 'listening' per its own L107-109 guard) and processRecognitionResult() (L147, reachable only after entering 'processing'). So after a single failed startListening() the assistant is permanently stuck in 'error' and every subsequent startListening() early-returns at L80 - the voice feature is bricked until the VoiceAssistant instance is recreated.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/voice/VoiceAssistant.ts:106-116 - same dead-end class for a transient stop failure: stopListening() awaits NativeSpeech.stopListening() (L112) with no try/catch, so if it rejects the state is left at 'listening' and never reaches L115 ('idle'); startListening() then permanently early-returns.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/hooks/usePushNotifications.ts:223-234 - setIsRegistered(true) is called at L223 BEFORE the backend registration await sendTokenToBackend(nativeToken.data) at L227. The surrounding try/catch (L230-234) only does setError(message) on failure and does not roll back isRegistered. So if the backend token-registration POST fails (network, 401, 5xx), the device reports isRegistered === true while the backend never stored the token - the UI/state believes push is active but the device will receive no server pushes, and nothing retries the backend registration.

Impact: silent push-delivery gap - a device shows as registered but is not reachable by the push-fanout pipeline (backend push_fanout). Lower severity (+1) because local notification permission really was granted and the error is surfaced via setError, but the isRegistered flag is misleading for any consumer that gates on it. Landable frontend-only fix: move setIsRegistered(true) to after sendTokenToBackend() resolves, or set it false / retry in the catch so the flag reflects backend state.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/widgets/WidgetDataProvider.ts:373-380 — private apiRequest<T>() wraps the whole fetch in try/catch and, on ANY error (rejected fetch = offline/timeout/DNS, or a thrown `API request failed: <status>` for a non-2xx), returns `{} as T` instead of re-throwing. The empty-object cast masks the failure from every caller.

Consequence: updateAllWidgets() (lines 136-160) deliberately wraps fetchWidgetData() in try/catch to classify each widget as `success: true/false` and only cache successful results. Because apiRequest never throws, the failure path is dead code — a failed backend fetch resolves to an empty payload, is treated as `success: true`, and gets written to AsyncStorage via cacheWidgetData(), OVERWRITING previously-valid cached widget data with empty data during a backend outage. Home-screen widgets then render blank/zeroed instead of showing stale-but-correct data or an error state.

Latent correctness concern that tests would pin: handleTap() (lines 163-225) only flips a granted result to denied inside `if (NativeNFC) { ... }`. When NativeNFC is null (native module unavailable), the transmit step is skipped but `validationResult.granted` stays true, so the code logs the attempt as 'granted' and calls updateCredentialUsage() even though no credential was physically transmitted to the reader. Reachability is uncertain (handleTap is invoked from the native module, which implies NFC present), hence medium confidence and a test-gap framing rather than a confirmed bug.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/accounting.rs:198-214,228-234 — because the date signal is absent, the tie-breaker set for VS-sharing invoices relies solely on amount + IBAN. For a tenant's recurring monthly invoices that share a variable symbol and amount (the common case for rent), nothing date-aware promotes the invoice whose period actually matches the payment date, so genuinely-equal-scoring candidates are all surfaced for manual resolution. Impact: weaker auto-reconciliation than FR-16.8 designs for -> more manual bank-line matching work. Landable backend-only fix: implement the date-proximity branch (e.g. small positive weight when |line.value_date - invoice.due_date| is within a window), keeping the clamped-to-1.0 confidence invariant at accounting.rs:221. Low severity (quality/completeness, not a crash).

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/delegations.rs:183-205 — create_delegation validates the target delegate ONLY for global existence (state.user_repo.find_by_id(req.delegate_user_id), the non-RLS repo), then creates the delegation. There is no check that req.delegate_user_id is a member of the delegator's organization (nor, for unit-scoped delegations, a co-owner/resident of the unit). The caller-side check at L207-236 only confirms the DELEGATOR owns the unit; the delegate is never org-gated.

Impact: an owner can delegate scopes 'voting' / 'financial' / 'documents' / 'faults' / 'all' (L158) to an arbitrary user from ANY other organization. Granting voting/financial authority inside an owners' association to a non-member is a cross-org privilege grant — the outside delegate can later act as the owner's proxy for governance and financial actions. The accept_delegation path (L432) only checks delegate_user_id == auth.user_id, so there is no downstream org gate either. Landable backend-only fix: after the existence check, verify the delegate shares the delegator's organization (org_member_repo.is_member) — mirror the is_member gate already used in unit_residents.rs authorize_unit_inner (L79-92) — and 400/403 otherwise. Confidence medium: end-to-end enforcement of the delegated scope was not traced at runtime (static review only).

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/unit_residents.rs:418-438 — add_resident (manager-gated via authorize_unit(..., require_manager=true)) validates the incoming req.user_id ONLY for global existence (state.user_repo.find_by_id(req.user_id).is_some()). It never verifies that req.user_id belongs to the unit's organization before calling unit_resident_repo.create (L452) with that user_id.

Impact: a manager can attach a user from a DIFFERENT organization as a resident of a unit in their building. The attached resident carries receives_notifications / receives_mail flags (L447-448) and a residency relationship to the unit, so the foreign user begins receiving that org's unit communications and is linked into the org's unit roster — cross-tenant data exposure / linkage. Contrast delegations.rs and energy.rs which both run an explicit membership gate; add_resident is missing it. Landable fix: gate req.user_id through org_member_repo.is_member(building.organization_id, req.user_id) (the org id already resolved inside authorize_unit) and reject with 400/404 when the target is not an org member. Confidence medium: downstream access conferred by residency was not runtime-traced.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/signatures.rs:116-119,184-189,199-205,231-237,357-363,371-378,703-712 — the signature-request handlers return ErrorResponse::new("DATABASE_ERROR", e.to_string()) on every DB error branch, interpolating the raw sqlx::Error Display straight into the client-facing response body. frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/registry/pages/RegistryPage.tsx:103-108, 123-131, 172-177, 191-201 — all four write mutation handlers (handlePetDelete, handlePetReview, handleVehicleDelete, handleVehicleReview) wrap mutateAsync in try/catch whose catch body is ONLY `console.error(...)`. RegistryPage.tsx never got the same treatment: it imports neither useToast nor any error-surface (grep of the file shows no useToast/showToast/setError), and the underlying hooks carry no central onError either — frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/registry/hooks/useRegistry.ts has zero onError/useToast/toast references, confirming the error is swallowed end-to-end.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/registry/pages/RegistryPage.tsx:87, 91, 137, 156, 160, 206 — all six intra-app navigations (view/edit/create for pets and vehicles) are done with `window.location.href = '/registry/...'`, triggering a full browser document reload inside what is a react-router SPA. Consequence: each 'View'/'Edit'/'Add' click tears down and re-bootstraps the whole React app — auth context re-init, TanStack Query cache discarded, i18n re-load, and a visible white flash — instead of a client-side route transition. It also makes the navigation untestable with the MemoryRouter used elsewhere and defeats SPA prefetch/state preservation. This is a correctness/UX smell, not just style, because it silently drops in-memory app state (e.g. unsaved filters on sibling screens) on every registry navigation.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:1156-1272 — the handler accepts a `SyncSessionRequest { pm_token, portal_session }` where both fields are supplied by the caller. When PM introspection says `active=true` AND the caller supplies ANY portal_session string that happens to be a live hash in `portal_sessions` for some OTHER user B, `refresh_session` returns Ok for B's session; the handler echoes B's session_token back as the 'synced' session for the pm_token's user A. No ownership cross-check gates this; the only consistency check is the `PM token inactive -> invalidate` branch at sso.rs:1179-1196.

Impact: correctness/confused-deputy. If a caller presents a pm_token for user A plus a portal_session for a different user B, the response says `{synced: true, session_token: <B's session>, refreshed: true, status: 'active'}`. A client that trusts 'this is now user A's session' will then issue B-authenticated requests while rendering A's identity — a cross-user identity mismatch the API makes no effort to detect. Marginal attack value is low (the caller must already hold B's live session), but the missing defense-in-depth check is landable: either look up the session's user_id and reject on mismatch (401) or always mint a fresh session for `user_info.user_id` and ignore the caller-supplied one. Backend-only, cloud-landable.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/listings.rs:856-877 — `POST /api/v1/listings/{id}/view` is wired via `record_view`; its `#[utoipa::path]` responses declare `(status = 204, 'View recorded')` AND `(status = 404, 'Listing not found')`, and the doc-comment explicitly says 'only return a hard error when the listing genuinely doesn't exist'. The body, however, is: `if let Err(e) = state.reality_portal_repo.track_view(id, "website").await { tracing::warn!(...); } Ok(axum::http::StatusCode::NO_CONTENT)` — no existence check, no 404 branch anywhere in the function. Calling it with a random UUID is indistinguishable from calling it with a real listing id; both return 204.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/listings.rs:63 — the route is registered as `.route("/{id}/view", axum::routing::post(record_view))`, so the discrepancy is user-visible: the generated OpenAPI/TS client expects a 404 variant that production never emits, and any client-side logic that gates on 404-vs-204 (e.g. 'did the user just click a stale link?') is silently dead code.

Impact: pure spec/impl drift — the fix is either (a) delete the 404 entry from the utoipa `responses(...)` + doc-comment to match the current always-204 behaviour, or (b) add a pre-check (`SELECT 1 FROM listings WHERE id=$1 AND status='active'`) before `track_view` and return 404 when it misses, matching the documented contract and giving monitors a signal that invalid IDs are being probed. Backend-only, cloud-landable. Confidence HIGH because the call path is trivial and the spec text is right beside the handler.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/state.rs:696-707 — in `TokenValidationCache::set`, after sweeping expired entries the fallback branch is guarded by `if cache.len() >= self.max_entries` and the comment reads `// If still full after eviction, remove oldest entries`. The implementation is `let keys_to_remove: Vec<String> = cache.iter().take(entries_to_remove).map(|(k,_)| k.clone()).collect();` — `cache` is a `HashMap<String, CachedTokenValidation>` (state.rs:622) and `HashMap::iter()` yields entries in an unspecified, hash-seed-dependent order. The effective eviction policy is therefore arbitrary, not LRU/oldest.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/state.rs:710-718 — nothing in `CachedTokenValidation { active, sub, scope, expires_at }` records insertion or last-access time, so any claim of 'oldest' cannot be satisfied without a schema change; the comment is strictly wrong today.

Impact: correctness smell on the hot SSO token-introspection cache (`AppState.token_cache`, used by every PM-token-bearing portal request via sso.rs:824-872). Under sustained cache saturation (10000 live PM tokens in the 60s TTL window — state.rs:633), a freshly-cached hit can be evicted ahead of one that has 1s left to live, forcing an unnecessary extra round-trip to PM `/oauth/introspect` and a `tracing::debug!("SSO token validation cache miss, calling PM API")` (sso.rs:835). Not a security issue (no privilege change, both paths re-check PM). Backend-only, cloud-landable: either align the comment ('remove arbitrary entries to make room') or record `inserted_at` on `CachedTokenValidation` and sort before evicting.
